column1: # premise-dairy: Plain, whole, cultured; milk and cultures are the only ingredients.

column4: Whole fat on the front; 'ultra-pasteurized' printed near the date means skip.
column5: Ultra-pasteurized means heated at or above 280 °F for at least 2 seconds, and WAPF lists ultrapasteurized milk products to avoid.

column4: Ingredient list reads milk and named cultures, with no sugar, pectin or flavors.
column5: Cornucopia notes certified organic yogurt can still carry a high amount of sugar, and plain organic tubs let the shopper add their own fruit; WAPF rates plain, whole yogurt as good.

column4: Skip when 'organic sugar' or 'natural flavors' sits in the ingredient list.
column5: WAPF lists sweetened yogurt and kefir under avoid, and Cornucopia scores yogurts on flavors, thickeners and the type of sweetener used.

column4: Whole milk kefir; ingredients are milk and kefir cultures.
column5: WAPF rates plain, whole yogurt and kefir without added vitamins, preferably grass-fed, as good.

column4: Ingredients: cream and cultures; no starch, gums or flavor words.
column5: WAPF lists sour cream with additives, and homogenized cream, under avoid.

column4: Cream is the only ingredient; 'ultra-pasteurized' not stamped on the carton.
column5: WAPF lists ultra-pasteurized cream under avoid; ultra-pasteurized means 280 °F for at least 2 seconds.

column4: Oil or sugar listed ahead of any dairy word in the ingredients.
column5: WAPF lists non-dairy creamers under avoid.

column4: Ingredients: cream, salt; skip any 'natural flavor' entry.
column5: WAPF rates pasteurized butter without natural flavors, preferably grass-fed, as good.

column4: Ingredient reads butterfat or clarified butter alone; no oil blended in.
column5: WAPF rates pasteurized ghee without natural flavors, preferably grass-fed, as good.

column4: Name reads 'cheese', never 'cheese food' or 'cheese product'.
column5: Pasteurized process cheese is cheeses ground and mixed with heat, a different standard of identity than the cheese itself.

column4: 'Pasteurized process cheese food' or 'cheese product' printed on the wrapper.
column5: Process cheese is comminuted and mixed with heat from one or more cheeses, not a single made cheese.

column4: Ingredients: cream, milk, salt, cultures; no gums or added thickeners.
column5: WAPF lists lowfat and fat-free cream cheese, and cream cheese made with additives, under avoid.

column4: Cultures named; carrageenan or gums not in the ingredient list.
column5: WAPF lists lowfat and fat-free cottage cheese, and cottage cheese made with additives, under avoid.

column4: Cream, milk, egg yolks and real vanilla; no 'flavor' words or extenders.
column5: WAPF rates simple flavors made with milk, cream, egg yolks and real vanilla as good and avoids extenders and natural flavors.

column4: Ingredients: milk and cultures only.
Ingredients: oats, water, salt; no added oil. Sweetened or seed-oil versions skip.
Ingredients: almonds and water; unsweetened. Sweetened or gum-and-oil blends skip.
Ingredients: organic soybeans and water. Soy protein isolate or sweetened versions skip.
Ingredients: coconut and water; unsweetened. Sweetened or oil-blend versions skip.
Can with coconut and water only; BPA-free lining stated.
column5: WAPF recommends canned whole coconut milk without additives, preferably in BPA-free containers.

column4: 'Vegetable oil' leads the ingredient list of any tub or stick.
column5: WAPF lists all margarines, spreads and partially hydrogenated shortenings under avoid.

column4: Palm, canola or 'vegetable oil blend' in the ingredient list.
column5: WAPF avoid list covers spreads combining butter with vegetable oils and most commercial vegetable and seed oils.

column4: 'Hydrogenated' or vegetable oil on a canned or tub topping.
column5: WAPF lists canned whipped cream and imitation whipped cream made with vegetable oils under avoid.

column1: # premise-oils: One named oil, dated and dark-bottled; unnamed vegetable oil blends are the skip.

column4: One oil named on the label: olive, coconut or avocado, not a blend.
column5: WAPF avoids most commercial vegetable and seed oils and lists extra virgin olive oil and avocado oil among good fats, so a single named oil is the alternative.

column4: Bottle reads 'vegetable oil' or lists soybean, canola, corn, cottonseed.
column5: WAPF avoid list names cottonseed, soy, corn and canola oils.

column4: Harvest date printed, dark glass or tin, 'extra virgin' on the front.
column5: UC Davis says dark glass, metal tins and bag-in-box protect oil from light and a harvest date shows freshness; WAPF lists extra virgin olive oil among good fats.

column4: Harvest or production date printed; virgin, not 'refined', on the label.
column5: UC Davis advises choosing avocado oil close to its harvest or production date, and WAPF lists avocado oil among good fats.

column4: 'Cold pressed' or 'expeller pressed' printed on the front of the bottle.
column5: Organic handling rules bar volatile synthetic solvents as processing aids.

column4: Lard or tallow the only ingredient; 'pastured' or 'grass-fed' on the label.
column5: WAPF rates lard from pigs raised outdoors and tallow from grass-fed cows and sheep as best fats.

column4: Smell of stale nuts or Play-Doh on opening; clear plastic bottle gets skipped.
column5: UC Davis names stale nuts or Play-Doh as the smell of rancid oil and clear plastic as least protective.

column1: # premise-grains-bread: One whole grain named first; sourdough over enriched; organic for glyphosate.

column4: Ingredient list is one grain, with 'whole' before its name.
column5: WAPF lists all non-organic grains and legumes, most sprayed with Roundup, under avoid.

column4: Ingredient reads whole grain oats; instant packets listing flavor or sugar fail.
column5: Organic bars excluded methods, and WAPF says grains are soaked, sprouted or fermented to neutralize phytic acid.

column4: Rice the only ingredient; brown rice syrup is a separate skip.
column5: WAPF rates organic whole grain rice among the best grains and lists white rice under avoid.

column4: Quinoa, millet or buckwheat the only ingredient; organic seal.
column5: WAPF lists all non-organic grains and legumes under avoid; MSU Extension lists millet as a whole grain.

column4: 'Wild rice' is the sole ingredient; no blend with white rice.
column5: WAPF rates wildcrafted wild rice as best and lists white rice under avoid; MSU Extension lists wild rice as a whole grain.

column4: USDA Organic seal on the bag; skip 'degerminated' cornmeal.
column5: Corn is on the Non-GMO Project High-Risk List, and the Whole Grains Council says degerminated corn meal never describes a whole grain.

column4: One legume named; soak-and-cook directions printed on the bag.
column5: WAPF rates organic dried beans and lentils as best, with grains and legumes soaked to minimize enzyme inhibitors and phytic acid.

column4: Dry bag lists beans alone; canned label states a BPA-free lining.
column5: WAPF rates organic dried beans as best and organic canned legumes as good, eaten only once or twice a month.

column4: Durum or whole wheat semolina named; no 'enriched' entry in the ingredients.
column5: WAPF rates organic whole grain pasta as good and lists white flour products including pasta under avoid.

column4: 'Whole wheat' on the bag; 'bleached' or 'enriched' flour means skip.
column5: WAPF says avoid white flour and white flour products, and lists bleached white flour under avoid.

column4: One flour named in the ingredient list; organic printed on the bag.
column5: WAPF rates freshly ground, soaked organic whole grain flours as best and organic sprouted flours as good.

column4: '100% whole grain' or 'whole' before the grain name; 'multigrain' alone is not enough.
column5: MSU Extension says multigrain is a mixture of grains, possibly all or mostly refined; the Whole Grains Council says it may describe refined grains.

column4: Extruded o's, flakes or puffs, or 'natural' printed on the box.
column5: WAPF lists extruded cold breakfast cereals under avoid, and Cornucopia flags misuse of the term natural on cereal.

column4: 'Sourdough' with a starter or culture named in the ingredients.
column5: WAPF rates sourdough bread from organic whole grain flour as best and says genuine sourdough fermentation breaks down gluten.

column4: 'Sprouted' before each grain in the ingredient list, not flour first.
column5: WAPF rates sourdough, soaked or sprouted breads from freshly ground organic whole grain flour as best.

column4: 'Enriched wheat flour', sugar or soybean oil near the top of the ingredient list.
column5: WAPF lists most commercial breads, based on white flour with hydrogenated oils, added gluten, soy or additives, under avoid.

column4: Skip unless the first ingredient names a flour with 'whole' before it.
column5: The Whole Grains Council says a first ingredient containing the word whole likely, though not surely, means a mostly whole grain product.

column4: Skip when ascorbic acid is listed; sourdough or sprouted on the bag passes.
column5: WAPF rates sourdough, soaked or sprouted breads from organic whole grain flour as best and lists breads containing ascorbic acid under avoid.

column1: # premise-sweeteners: Name the sweetener on the label; unnamed sugar and syrups are the skip.

column4: 'Dehydrated cane juice' or organic cane sugar named, not 'sugar' alone.
column5: WAPF lists dehydrated sugar cane juice among best sweeteners and white sugar under avoid.

column4: 'Pure maple syrup' only; corn syrup in the ingredients means imitation.
column5: WAPF lists maple syrup as a best sweetener and imitation syrups under avoid.

column4: 'Raw' and 'unfiltered' on the jar; cloudy with pollen, not clear.
column5: Ultra-filtration removes all pollen, and pollen is the only sure way to trace honey to a place.

column4: Ingredient reads molasses or dehydrated cane juice, no 'sugar' ahead of it.
column5: WAPF names molasses and dehydrated sugar cane juice among its best sweeteners.

column4: Sweetener named by its plant in the ingredients, not 'natural sweetener'.
column5: WAPF lists organic coconut sugar, palm sugar and date sugar among its best natural sweeteners.

column4: Corn syrup, agave or brown rice syrup anywhere in the ingredients.
column5: WAPF avoid list names corn syrup, high fructose corn syrup, brown rice syrup and agave.

column1: # premise-nuts-seeds: Raw or dry-roasted, sealed, ingredient list is the nut or seed alone.

column4: Sealed package, ingredient list the nut alone; skip open bins.
column5: WAPF rates fresh organic raw nuts in sealed packages, not from bins, as best.

column4: 'Raw' printed on a sealed pack; coated or sugared nuts mean skip.
column5: WAPF rates fresh organic raw nuts in sealed packages as best and lists nut mixtures with sugar, agave or flavorings under avoid.

column4: Ingredients: nuts, maybe salt; sugar, palm or 'hydrogenated' words mean skip.
column5: WAPF avoid list covers nut butters with hydrogenated oils, sugar, agave or flavorings.

column4: Raw seeds sealed with a date; the seed is the lone ingredient.
column5: WAPF rates fresh organic raw seeds in sealed packages as best.

column4: Sugar, chocolate or vegetable oil listed beside the nuts.
column5: WAPF avoid list names nut mixtures with partially hydrogenated oils, sugar, chocolate or flavorings.

column4: Flakes list yeast alone in the ingredients.

column1: # premise-canned-jarred: Glass or stated BPA-free cans; ingredients are the food, salt, named oil.

column4: Label states BPA-free lining; ingredients are the food, water, salt.
column5: WAPF rates canned organic tomato products in BPA-free containers as good and lists most canned fruits and vegetables under avoid.

column4: Tomatoes first, oil named; no sugar or 'natural flavors' listed.
column5: WAPF lists most commercial sauces, ketchup and other condiments under avoid.

column4: Glass jar; vegetables, oil by name, salt and spices, nothing else.
column5: WAPF lists most commercial sauces, ketchup and other condiments under avoid.

column4: Sea vegetable named alone; country of origin printed, and not China.
column5: WAPF rates whole or powdered sea vegetables not from China as best and lists seaweed from China, even organic, under avoid.

column4: Chickpeas, tahini, olive oil named; canola or soybean oil means skip.
column5: WAPF avoid list names canola and soy oils.

column1: # premise-snacks-condiments: Short list you could stock yourself; no natural flavors, no unnamed oil.

column4: One herb named on the jar; no blend listing citric acid or MSG.
column5: WAPF avoid list covers spices and blends containing MSG, citric acid or hydrolyzed protein.

column4: Whole seeds or sticks of one spice named; no 'spices' blend.
column5: WAPF lists spices and blends containing MSG, citric acid, hydrolyzed protein or other additives under avoid.

column4: Grey, pink, red or beige colour; 'iodized' on the label means skip.
column5: WAPF lists unrefined salt in light grey, pink, red or beige as best and iodized salt as avoid.

column4: 'Aluminum-free' printed on the tin.
column5: WAPF lists aluminum-free baking powder as best and baking powder containing aluminum under avoid.

column4: 'Raw' and 'unfiltered' printed; cloudy strands of mother at the bottom.
column5: WAPF lists organic raw vinegars as best.

column4: 'Distilled white vinegar' printed; apple cider, wine or balsamic named passes.
column5: WAPF avoid list names distilled vinegar.

column4: Tomatoes, vinegar, spices listed; no 'natural flavors' entry.
column5: WAPF lists organic mustard and organic fermented ketchup among best condiments.

column4: Naturally fermented or brewed on the label; liquid amino acids mean skip.
column5: WAPF lists organic raw naturally fermented soy sauce among best and liquid amino acids under avoid.

column4: Soybean or canola oil named as the first oil on the label.
column5: WAPF avoid list names soy and canola oils.

column4: Skip when white flour, hydrogenated oil or soy flour is listed.
column5: WAPF lists most commercial crackers based on white flour with partially hydrogenated oils, soy flour or additives under avoid.

column4: Skip when refined white flour leads the ingredient list.
column5: WAPF lists white flour products under avoid.

column4: Brown rice syrup, agave or soy protein isolate in the ingredients means skip.
column5: WAPF lists brown rice syrup and agave under avoid and says soy protein isolate carries natural toxins and ones created in processing.

column4: Potatoes or corn, olive or coconut oil named, salt; nothing else.
column5: WAPF lists most commercial vegetable and seed oils under avoid and olive and organic virgin coconut oil among best.

column4: Puffed grain with flavor coating, 'natural flavor' or syrup in ingredients.
column5: WAPF lists puffed grain products such as rice cakes under avoid.

column1: # premise-beverages: Water, tea, coffee beans; sugar or natural flavors listed means skip.

column4: 'Spring water' printed on the label.
column5: Spring water must be collected only at the spring or through a bore hole tapping the underground formation feeding the spring.

column4: Organic seal on the coffee bag.
column5: Cornucopia says harmful chemicals banned in the U.S. are still widely used on coffee abroad, and recommends USDA certified organic.

column4: Leaves or herbs named alone; 'natural flavors' not in the ingredients.
column5: Federal rules define natural flavor as including essential oil, extractive and any product of roasting, heating or enzymolysis.

column4: 'From concentrate' or 'juice cocktail' on the front, sugar listed.
column5: WAPF lists fruit and vegetable juices under avoid.

column4: Sugar, caramel color or 'natural flavors' in the ingredients.
column5: WAPF lists soft drinks and beverages containing natural flavors under avoid.

column4: Organic on the label, in a glass bottle; black tea listed.
column5: WAPF recommends organic lacto-fermented beverages in glass jars, such as kombucha made with organic black tea.

column4: Coconut water the sole ingredient; aseptic box means skip.
column5: WAPF lists coconut products in aseptic boxes under avoid.
